title: Hide a ball under the middle cup, watch the three cups being shuffled, then lift only the cup that hides it
instruction: Play the cups-and-ball game. First hide the red ball under the middle cup: lift the middle cup with one hand and hold it up while the other hand takes the ball from the dish and puts it on the middle ring, then lower the cup over it. Press the start button and keep both arms where they started while the cups are shuffled: the lamp blinks amber, then the cups glide around and swap places, and the lamp turns green when they stop. Then lift the cup the ball is under (the first cup you lift must be that one) and hold it up while the other hand takes the ball out. Set the cup back down on its ring, put the ball back in the dish and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Keeping track of a hidden object while it is moved around is a basic piece of memory that people and animals use all the time: the cups look exactly alike once they stop, so a policy that acts only on what it sees now picks the right cup one time in three.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A green felt mat 6 mm thick with a gold border, from 10 to 40 cm forward and 22.5 cm to each side of the centre line, fixed, with three white rings 9.2 cm across printed on it in a row 26 cm forward: the middle one on the centre line and the others 10 cm to its left and right; in the middle of each ring a ball seat of eight felt nubs 3 mm tall on a circle 2.1 cm across. (2) Three identical copper cups (90 g each), mouth down, one on each ring: 6 cm tall, 8 cm across at the flared mouth and 5.4 cm across the straight foot band at the top, with three brass beads; they are hollow. (3) A small white porcelain dish 8 cm across and 1.4 cm deep with a blue band, fixed, 15.5 cm forward on the centre line, holding (4) a red ball 1.9 cm across (12 g). (5) A black start console 7 cm square and 3 cm tall, fixed, its middle 16 cm forward and 17 cm left of the centre line, with a red start button 3.4 cm across on a spring (8 mm of travel) and a lamp in front of it. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot; only the shuffle differs, with the trial's seed.
scoring: Watched every control step. The shuffle starts 5 s after the start button is pushed 4 mm down (the lamp blinks amber); the cups then make five swaps of 1.4 s with 0.35 s between them (two neighbouring cups trade places, one passing 6 cm behind the row and the other 3.5 cm in front of it), the ball moving with the cup it is under (centred under it as the shuffle starts), and the lamp turns green. A cup counts as lifted once its mouth is 1 cm above the mat or it tips over 15 degrees; the ball is under a cup when it lies on the mat within 3.6 cm of the cup's middle. 0.0 whatever else (latched): the ball arrived on the middle ring while the middle cup was not lifted; a gripper's fingertip centre went more than 8 cm from where it started while the cups were moving; the first cup lifted after the shuffle was not the ball's cup; or the ball came out from under its cup after the shuffle (more than 3.6 cm from where it lay, or lifted) while that cup was not lifted. 1.0: the ball in the dish, all three cups mouth down on the three rings (each within 2.5 cm of a ring's middle, tipped less than 8 degrees), and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the ball in the dish, taken out while its cup was lifted; 0.5: at some point the first cup lifted after the shuffle was the ball's cup; 0.25: at some point the shuffle ran with the ball under the middle cup and all three cups on their rings; else 0.0. Judged at the end of the trial, which ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the cups and the ball still.
reset_notes: Put the three cups back on their rings and the ball back in the dish; the lamp goes dark at every reset. The swaps are drawn from the trial's seed.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the shuffle is a rule standing in for the mat's hidden shuffler: the task file moves the cups, and the ball under one, centred, along fixed arcs each control step, from the trial's seed. Each cup is a cone of 28 flat copper panels; the button is a sprung cap and the lamp a coloured disc. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
